questions.title: Planning an experiment — capacitor discharge current and plate separation

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer:
Diagram: d.c. supply connected through the reed switch to a parallel-plate capacitor; resistor in series with an ammeter (to measure I); voltmeter across the d.c. supply (to measure E); signal generator or a.c. supply connected to terminals F and G of the reed switch; the two circular plates (area A, separation h) supported on stands (vertical orientation) or on the bench with spacers (horizontal orientation).
Procedure and measurements: vary h (independent variable) and measure I (dependent variable); measure h with calipers or a micrometer — measure the total distance between the outer faces of the plates and subtract the plate thicknesses; read I on the ammeter for each value of h; repeat the measurement of h at several positions between the plates and take the mean; use a range of at least 5–6 values of h.
Analysis: plot a graph of I against 1/h; the relationship I = KAfE/h is valid if a straight line through the origin is obtained; gradient = K/(AfE), so K = gradient × AfE (or plot lg I against lg h — a straight line of gradient −1; then K = AfE × 10^intercept).
Controls: keep f constant (fixed signal-generator setting); keep A and E constant; measure the diameter d of the plates with calipers and calculate A = πd²/4; determine f with an oscilloscope — measure the period T from the time-base (T = number of divisions × time-base setting, or time for n cycles divided by n) and calculate f = 1/T — or read it off the signal generator; keep the plates parallel and aligned using spacers of equal thickness and check h at different points on the plates; use large values of A to increase I and reduce the percentage uncertainty in I.
Safety: clamp the stands to the bench so the plates cannot fall; avoid electric shock — do not touch the plates or capacitor terminals and switch off the circuit when adjusting h; do not touch the resistor when hot; place an insulating mat on the bench.

questions.title: Oscillations of a suspended rod — period versus string separation

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer:
Squaring the equation: T² = 4π²αD/(MgL²) = (4π²αD/Mg) × 1/L²
Comparing with y = mx: gradient = 4π²αD/(Mg)

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer:
All six points from (b) plotted correctly — each within half a small square of its true position, with point diameter less than half a small square (check the second and fifth plots from the left; ecf from 2(b)).
Error bars in T² plotted for all six points — total length of each bar accurate to less than half a small square and symmetrical about the point.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer:
Straight line of best fit drawn (not from the top point to the bottom point; line thickness less than half a small square; must pass between (5.0, 1.0) and (5.3, 1.0) and between (11.3, 2.2) and (11.6, 2.2)).
Worst acceptable line drawn — the steepest or shallowest line that passes through all the error bars (may be constrained by an intermediate error bar).
Label both lines.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.answer:
Using two widely spaced points on the best-fit line (Δx at least 7), with clear substitution into Δy/Δx:
gradient = (2.50 − 0.64)/(13.32 − 3.28) = 1.86/10.04 = 0.185 (expect about 0.14 − 0.24)
Absolute uncertainty = gradient(best fit) − gradient(worst acceptable line), or ½(steepest gradient − shallowest gradient) = ± 0.02
gradient = 0.185 ± 0.02 s² m²

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.answer:
α = gradient × Mg/(4π²D) = 0.185 × 0.097 × 9.81/(4π² × 0.825) = 0.176/32.6
= 5.4 × 10⁻³ kg m² (expect about 5.5 × 10⁻³; 2–3 s.f.; ecf from 2(c)(iii) and 2(d))
Unit of α: kg m² (or g m²)

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.answer:
%unc(α) = (Δgradient/gradient + 2ΔD/D + ΔM/M) × 100%
= (0.02/0.185 + 2 × 0.004/0.825 + 2/97) × 100%
= (10.8% + 1.0% + 2.1%) = 13.8% (answer must be greater than 2.5%; max/min method allowed)

parts.label: (f)
parts.answer:
T² = gradient/L², so L = √(gradient)/T
L = √0.185/2.20 = 0.430/2.20 = 0.196 m, i.e. about 0.20 m (minimum 2 s.f.; ecf from 2(c)(iii))
ΔL/L = ½ × Δgradient/gradient + ΔT/T = ½ × 0.02/0.185 + 0.02/2.20 = 0.054 + 0.009 = 0.063
ΔL = 0.063 × 0.196 = 0.012 m
L = (0.196 ± 0.012) m, i.e. about 0.20 ± 0.01 m
(or using α: L = 2π√(αD/(Mg))/T with ΔL/L = ½(Δα/α) + ΔT/T, Δα/α from 2(e)(ii))
